_description: Knowledge base for LLM hallucination detection and mitigation, curated for MLGG extraction pipeline hardening.

hallucination_types.description: LLM invents values not present in source text (e.g., fabricated AUROC, patient count)
LLM returns semantically similar but schema-invalid values (e.g., 'moderate' instead of 'medium')
Extracted numbers are internally contradictory (e.g., events + non-events != total)
LLM makes unsupported inferential judgments (e.g., leakage risk assessment without evidence)
LLM returns null for fields that are clearly stated in the text
mitigation: explicit instruction to extract all available fields

implemented_in_mlgg.description: Pydantic Literal types reject non-allowed categorical values at parse time
model_post_init checks arithmetic consistency, CI ordering, range bounds
4 *_evidence fields require LLM to cite paper text for boolean leakage determinations
implemented_in_mlgg.effectiveness: enables human audit; does not prevent fabricated quotes
transparency layer; downstream consumers can differentiate LLM vs human data

recommended_additions.description: Run extraction N times (N>=3), take majority vote per field. Disagreements flag potential hallucination.
recommended_additions.complexity: low (N API calls per paper, no new infrastructure)
recommended_additions.expected_improvement: significant for numeric fields and boolean judgments

recommended_additions.description: Check that *_evidence strings actually appear (fuzzy match) in the source paper text.
Verify extracted numbers (AUROC, n_patients, etc.) appear in the paper text via regex.
Separate LLM call or rule-based module verifies claims without seeing extraction prompt.
10-20 manually annotated papers as regression test set for extraction accuracy.
recommended_additions.expected_improvement: enables quantitative tracking of extraction quality over time

key_statistics.cot_improvement: 86.4% of comparisons showed reduced hallucination with chain-of-thought (Kim 2025)
